rows.claim: Gabriel cannot be overpowered, obstructed, or deceived by devils; his strength and direct access to God secure his mission, as also described in al-Najm.

rows.speaker: author

rows.anchor: when this word occurs before an attribute, it is meant to highlight the grandeur and importance of that attribute.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel's emphasized trustworthiness ensures that he conveys God's revelation unchanged, unlike the thieves and liars behind soothsayer lore.
rows.anchor: it is this attribute which ensures that whatever Gabriel brings from God to the Prophet (sws) is absolutely free of any alteration

rows.anchor: His only responsibility is to warn them through these signs even if they are not able to see them. He cannot guide the blind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's historical examples show that God controls individuals and nations, gives respite as He wills, and seizes them when their term ends; none can exceed His limits.
rows.anchor: Similar is His dealing with nations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Favours and deprivation test whether people become grateful and fulfill others' rights or grow conceited, and whether they remain content or despair; the peaceful soul succeeds.
rows.anchor: He is testing whether blessing someone with favours makes him grateful

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fates of powerful nations prove God's control: after respite, those who cross His limits are seized helplessly despite their power and glory.
rows.anchor: When they wrongly use their freedom to exercise their will and cross the limits set for them by the Almighty, they are given respite

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People wrongly interpret prosperity as proof of divine honor and reduced livelihood as humiliation; both are tests under God's law.
rows.anchor: is governed by the Almighty’s law of trial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prosperity tests gratitude and care for others rather than pride and usurpation; hardship tests contentment rather than despair, and people should examine their treatment of orphans and the poor.

rows.claim: The oaths establish that God alone governs the world, brings things forth and removes them, grants respite, and acts within no rival's authority.
